scope: Targeted verification of the supplied manuscript’s five cited works. No comparison with other essays and no broad novelty campaign.

sources.title: In Defence of Second-Order Reasons
sources.result: The inference to some judges excluding considerations in deliberation is present. Footnote 39 gives a sufficient route; footnote 43 allows other forms of guidance. The manuscript represents these qualifications accurately.
sources.limitations: Targeted passages, not an audit of the whole theory. DOI resolver failed; publisher HTML succeeded.

sources.title: Binding Hercules: A Proposal for Bench Trials
sources.result: The text explicitly distinguishes discounting from discarding, discusses the insignificant exposed-group difference, and links residual reliance to improper decision bases. The manuscript gives this predecessor appropriate credit.
sources.limitations: No broad novelty search. This is primary evidence for Wittlin’s own argument, not independent primary verification of the 2005 experiment.

sources.title: Responding to second-order reasons
sources.type: primary philosophical article, published PDF in author institution repository
sections_checked: introductory statement of causal and appraisal requirements
sources.result: A reminder of a promise changes the basis while the decision can remain fixed. The causal/appraisal description also matches.
sources.limitations: Publisher DOI/full-text requests failed; UNED repository copy succeeded. No attempt to adjudicate the entire basing theory.

sources.authors: Leonard Hoeft; Michael Kurschilgen; Wladislaw Mill
sources.title: Norms as Obligations
sources.type: primary experimental working paper, research consortium PDF
sources.result: A modified dictator game lets participants reveal unknown recipient payoffs; authoritative requests affect this search. Section 6 discusses alternative explanations.
sources.limitations: Working-paper version is the substantive source used, as in the manuscript; data and statistical analysis were not replicated.

sources.title: Can Judges Ignore Inadmissible Information? The Difficulty of Deliberately Disregarding
sources.type: original primary research article reproduced in publicly accessible third-party text
sources.result: The reproduction matches all three counts, the self-formed admissibility subgroups, Fisher p=.42, the possible probative-value difference, the admitted-evidence instruction, and the earlier confidence result.
sources.limitations: Official full text was inaccessible. The readable copy is a third-party transcription with star pagination, not an authenticated publisher PDF. Counts are also corroborated by Wittlin n.143, except that 27/55 is explicit only in this reproduction.
